subject: bottlenose dolphin
title: Dolphins Trap Fish in Giant Seashells, Then Shake Them Out

scenes.text: Some dolphins hunt with a seashell. And they don't learn it from their mothers.
In Shark Bay, Western Australia, fish hide inside big empty sea snail shells.
A dolphin pushes its beak into the opening, lifts the shell to the surface, and shakes it.
The fish slides straight into its mouth.
Over 11 years, researchers saw 19 dolphins out of more than a thousand do it.
Most dolphin skills pass from mother to calf. This one spreads between friends, the way it does in apes.

description:
Dolphins in Shark Bay, Western Australia, chase fish into empty giant sea snail shells, carry the shell to the surface and shake the fish into their mouths. It's called shelling.
Between 2007 and 2018 researchers logged 42 shelling events by 19 of 1,035 dolphins. Unlike most dolphin foraging skills, which pass from mother to calf, shelling spreads between associates, like tool skills in great apes. The study was published in Current Biology in 2020.
What's the smartest animal hunting trick you've seen?
first_comment: Shelling was first spotted in the mid-1990s and is still rare. Which animal would you want to learn a trick from?
